newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentina to repay early $750 mln to Paris Club.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to repay early $750 mln to Paris Club.

text.p: Argentina will repay early $750 million of its Paris Club debt, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Tuesday.
"We're going to pay back in advance $750 million to the Paris Club within our 1997 budget," Fernandez told Reuters on the fringes of the annual meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank.
Fernandez gave no details on the timing of the repayment, but added, "That's the decision we've taken and we're going to start to carry it out."
Argentina is eagerly trying to improve its international credit rating in order to reduce its borrowing costs.
Fernandez made the announcement on the Paris Club debt repayment during a brief break in a meeting with the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) Director for the western hemisphere, Claudio Loser.
Argentina hopes to reach an agreement with the IMF on an extended fund facility to replace the stand-by loan programme it has had since 1995.

After the meeting, Loser told reporters that talks with Argentina were on the right track. He added that there was no rush to complete a deal since Argentina has returned on a firm footing to international capital markets since the 1994 peso crisis.
Loser added that he thought Argentina's decision to repay in advance the Paris Club debt was "a very good thing" and that it should help the country manage its debt portfolio.
